syllabusTopics: Potential difference, potential due to a point charge, potential energy, electron volt
agentNotes: Authoring contract: frontend/AGENTS.md §9 (extra unit card). Exam bank: volt MCQ (2023), W-V-n derivation (2022).

card.title: Exam bank — every board question on electric potential

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Two questions: one volt equals one joule per coulomb (2023 MCQ) and the W-V-n electron relation derivation (2022). Potential is work per charge; the electron-volt prices atomic energies (1 eV = 1.6x10^-19 J); field is the downhill gradient E = -dV/dr.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: V = W/q, 1 V = 1 J/C · V = kQ/r · U = qV · W = n e V · 1 eV = 1.6x10^-19 J · E = -dV/dr

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: V = kQ/r pins zero at infinity (meaning isolated-charge convention). W = neV counts elementary charges only (alpha particles carry 2e). Equipotential-perpendicular field geometry needs electrostatics.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: MCQ answer (b) joule per coulomb — joule alone, newton, ampere all die on units. Hollow-conductor interior: constant V, zero E (shielding). Electrons run uphill in V (negative charge).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: NEB 2022 (4): each electron crossing V gains eV, so n electrons do W = neV (e.g. 10^18 electrons over 100 V move 16 J). NEB 2023 (1): volt defined as joule per coulomb — unit analysis alone selects (b).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Mark-losers: volt equated with joule (per-coulomb missing); eV treated as voltage instead of energy; absolute potential quoted without zero convention. Time-varying fields break scalar-potential reasoning.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Test charge from infinity against kQ/r2 integrates to V = kQ/r. Field from potential: dV = -E dr along the field, so E = -dV/dr (downhill). Equipotentials follow as constant-V contours cut squarely by field lines.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: '1 volt =' means joule per coulomb, instantly. Energy: count charges times e times volts. Equipotentials sketched first, field lines perpendicular second.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (1): volt equals J/C (MCQ). NEB 2022 (4): W from V and n electrons. That is the complete bank.
